text:
Tyler Bertuzzi scored 32 goals for Chicago last season. Through 19 games this year he has two, he is pointless in five straight, and the local coverage has noticed: the Chicago Sun-Times asked "why Tyler Bertuzzi's goal-scoring has disappeared," and Bleacher Nation wrote that the Blackhawks need more from him.

The honest answer is some of each. His team has scored 5.7 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which is bad luck, and that usually swings back. But his own chances have thinned out too: 1.5 expected goals on his shots over his last ten against 2.6 usual, and his expected goals per 60 sit at 0.65, against 1.25 last season. The Blackhawks have lost eight of his last ten games.

Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among all forwards last season at 2.8 wins above replacement, driving play while skating with some of the weakest teammates in the league. The Athletic's Scott Powers noted a lineup change this week, with Frank Nazar taking his net-front spot on a goal. What to watch: whether he gets back to the dirty areas where his goals live.
headline: Tyler Bertuzzi's goals have gone missing in Chicago
